text: **vs. Rony Meisler — the founder whose autonomy Jatahy's philosophy was supposed to protect.** Meisler's Reserva became part of the Azzas 2154 group via the Arezzo side of the 2024 merger, then was caught directly in the Birman-Jatahy reorganization fight — the very brand Jatahy's May-2026 injunction fought to keep under continuity rather than see reassigned. Meisler and Reserva's other founders exited the company during the integration turmoil regardless. The disagreement is less about a stated position and more a structural one: Jatahy's public doctrine says a roll-up should let the founder's "alma" run the brand, but even the executive publicly committed to that doctrine could not, in practice, prevent Reserva's founding team from leaving once centralizing pressure from the other side of the merger took hold. See Meisler's own dossier for the founder-side account of that same integration.
title: vs. Rony Meisler — the founder whose autonomy Jatahy's philosophy was supposed to protect

text: **vs. Warren Buffett — shared instincts on cash discipline, opposite instincts on integration.** Both prize idle cash over a forced deal and distrust debt-fueled growth: Jatahy's "prefiro ter 600, 700 milhões parados" echoes Buffett's fortress-balance-sheet doctrine. But Buffett's model is to buy rarely and then leave existing management almost entirely alone; Jatahy's model runs a much higher deal cadence (Hering, ByNV, NV, and a standing "sweet spot" numeric filter) and is far more actively involved in post-deal brand strategy (megastores, channel unification, creative succession planning) than Buffett's hands-off style would sanction.

title: vs. Warren Buffett — shared instincts on cash discipline, opposite instincts on integration

text: **The autonomy-preserving model didn't protect its own author.** Jatahy's entire M&A doctrine is built on not imposing a boss on an acquired founder — yet when he became the subordinate co-founder in a merger he didn't fully control, he needed a court injunction to avoid exactly that treatment from Birman. The philosophy that worked when he held the controlling chair did not automatically generalize to when he didn't. (Money Times, mai/2026; Mercado&Consumo, mai/2026)
title: The autonomy-preserving model didn't protect its own author

text: **Personal-conduct critique from named market sources: "o Roberto não quer ter chefe."** Multiple investors quoted anonymously by NeoFeed attribute the Birman conflict specifically to Jatahy's own resistance to hierarchy/subordination, not just to legitimate strategic disagreement — a diagnosis made in March 2025, over a year before the 2026 injunction, suggesting market participants saw the pattern coming. A separate anonymous source goes further, calling him "muito orgulhoso e uma pessoa muito difícil... a razão pela qual nenhum executivo de ponta tem ficado no grupo," pointing to roughly 30 non-executive director departures and two rounds of retention packages since the merger as corroborating evidence. Independent retail-trade reporting names concrete exits as symptoms of the same tension — Rony Meisler (Reserva's founder) and Paulo Kruglensky, the executive charged with integrating the two groups, who left roughly six months into the job — a churn pattern visible over a year before the 2026 injunction. (NeoFeed, mar/2025; NeoFeed, mai/2026; Central do Varejo, mar/2025)

text: **Broken integration timeline on the group's largest deal.** He publicly promised Hering would be "completamente repaginada em 30 a 36 meses" from mid-2021 — i.e., by roughly mid-2024. In October 2022 (16 months in), InfoMoney reported the company still couldn't deliver 27% of what it sold to multibrand retailers and franchises against a sector target of 10%, and explicitly named a capability gap: "Dono da Farm e da Animale, o Soma não tinha experiência com produtos de maior volume e baixo custo." By March 2024, the group booked a R$2.9bn accounting write-down on Hering's assets — larger than analysts expected — even as the CFO denied overpaying. (InfoMoney, out/2022; Exame INSIGHT, mar/2024)

text: Rodrigo Vidigal is the president of Motorola Mobility Brazil (since September 2023, succeeding José Cardoso), and the clearest documented voice in Brazilian tech-business press for a specific, repeated thesis: Brazil is not just Motorola's second- or third-largest consumer market but a "global laboratory" whose engineers, product features and go-to-market experiments get exported to the rest of the company — a claim he backs with a named example (the Brazilian-invented Foto Guiada camera feature) rather than leaving it abstract. His operating register is numbers-forward and sequencing-driven: resolve the brand's "rational" trust attributes before spending on "aspirational" ones, hold intermediate-market share while pushing deliberately into premium and ultra-premium price bands, and prefer external best-of-breed partnerships (Bose, Sony, Corning, Pantone, Swarovski) over building every capability in-house. His sharpest single framing is that leadership is a perception problem before it is a volume one — "Eu preciso ser número um na cabeça do consumidor" — and he is unusual for this corpus in citing a hard, moving brand-consideration number to back the claim (superpremium consideration up from 49% to 73%, Tecnoblog). He is a company operator rather than a founder-philosopher — his boldest documented heuristic is procedural (launch under regulatory ambiguity, formalize compliance after, learned from bringing Brazil's first prepaid mobile plan to market in 1998) rather than ideological — and the corpus is almost entirely friendly, institutional press coverage: only the Tecnoblog factory-visit Q&A (Nov 2023) puts genuine follow-up pushback to him ("Não deu certo?", "Não tem aparelho demais?"), and the sharpest available critique of Motorola's Brazilian product strategy (Canaltech, camera and software-update gaps) predates his presidency and never names him. He sits opposite Manoel Conde Neto's vertical-integration instinct and shares, from an unrelated starting point, Jensen Huang's ecosystem-over-ownership logic.

text: Rodrigo Vidigal became president of Motorola Mobility Brazil in September 2023, succeeding José Cardoso, who was promoted to lead the company's Latin America operation; the global CEO of Motorola/Lenovo's mobile business, Sergio Buniac, is also Brazilian, a fact Vidigal's interviewers treat as reinforcing the idea that Brazilian leadership carries disproportionate weight inside the global company (NeoFeed). His career predates Motorola: in 1998, while an executive at CTBC (later absorbed into Algar Telecom), he was involved in launching Brazil's first prepaid mobile phone plan at a moment when no regulatory framework for prepaid service yet existed, operating for a period under a provisional license with monthly reporting to Anatel (Tele.Síntese). By the time he is describing Motorola's Brazilian operation in the press, he frames the 2009 Brazilian launch of Android — while already at Motorola — as a formative moment that raised the Brazilian team's internal standing within the global company (Tele.Síntese), a beat that recurs across nearly every subsequent interview in different phrasing: Brazil as Motorola's third-largest market worldwide (Tele.Síntese), fourth-largest smartphone market in the world (Mobile Time), and "a maior exportadora de tecnologia para o mundo" within the company's R&D network, with more than 1,200 engineers (Bloomberg Línea). Under his presidency Motorola has run a consistent, publicly stated market-share-growth and premiumization program — from roughly 10% premium share early in a fiscal year to "15% a 18%" (Bloomberg Línea, Dec/2024) to a stated ambition of 30% market share overall by end of 2026 (Forbes Brasil, Mar/2026) — while also publicly naming gray-market/contraband smuggling, not Chinese OEM competition, as the company's top strategic worry (Forbes Brasil). His earliest post-appointment interview in the corpus (Tecnoblog, Nov/2023), given during a factory visit in Jaguariúna and pegged to the tenth anniversary of the Moto G line and its 200-millionth unit sold, is where he defines the goal most concretely: not raw volume but mindshare ("Eu preciso ser número um na cabeça do consumidor"), quantified by an internal research figure — superpremium purchase-consideration for the Motorola brand rising from 49% to 73% — and by a candid diagnosis that credit access, not product, is "o maior problema do varejo no Brasil" after Brazilian interest rates "saltou de 2% ao ano para aproximadamente 13%" (Tecnoblog).

Eu preciso ser número um na cabeça do consumidor
o maior problema do varejo no Brasil

text: **Brazil is Motorola's laboratory, not just its market.** The clearest, most repeated framing in the corpus: "O Brasil é o quarto maior mercado de smartphones do mundo, é extremamente relevante e dita tendências globais." [Brazil is the fourth-largest smartphone market in the world, it's extremely relevant and it sets global trends.] (Mobile Time) He backs the claim with a specific, named worked example rather than leaving it as a boast: the Foto Guiada camera feature on the razr 70, razr 70 ultra and razr Fold — a tool that lets a user photograph a horizon they want to keep, then hands the phone to someone else to re-shoot the same framing by matching a transparent overlay of the earlier image — was created by a Brazilian, Mauricio Moisés, Motorola's senior camera-products manager (Mobile Time). The same idea recurs as a market-hierarchy claim, not just a product one: "Hoje, o Brasil é o terceiro maior mercado da Motorola no mundo e abriga lideranças que atuam internacionalmente." [Today, Brazil is Motorola's third-largest market in the world and is home to leaders who operate internationally.] (Tele.Síntese) — and again as an R&D-export claim: "Hoje, a operação brasileira é a maior exportadora de tecnologia para o mundo. O nosso investimento em P&D conta com mais de 1.200 engenheiros que desenvolvem inovação, inteligência artificial, e exportam esse know-how." [Today, the Brazilian operation is the biggest exporter of technology in the world. Our R&D investment includes more than 1,200 engineers who develop innovation, artificial intelligence, and export that know-how.] (Bloomberg Línea) A third, non-product instance sharpens the thesis into something falsifiable rather than rhetorical: NeoFeed reports that in 2021 Brazil was "palco do projeto-piloto da empresa no varejo" — the stage for Motorola's global retail pilot — before that store/kiosk model was extended to other markets, and names Brazil as one of the company's three largest markets worldwide alongside the United States and India (which is also the likely reconciliation of the "third-largest" claim: third among Motorola's markets, versus fourth among all smartphone markets globally). So the "laboratory" claim is backed by three differently-shaped proof points — a product feature (Foto Guiada), a retail/go-to-market format (the 2021 pilot), and an organizational milestone (the 2009 Android launch) — not one anecdote stretched three ways. Note the internal inconsistency in rank ("third" vs. "fourth" largest market) across two interviews — recorded, and now partially reconciled by the NeoFeed US/India/Brazil framing, in *Blind spots*.

Hoje, a operação brasileira é a maior exportadora de tecnologia para o mundo. O nosso investimento em P&D conta com mais de 1.200 engenheiros que desenvolvem inovação, inteligência artificial, e exportam esse know-how.

title: Brazil is Motorola's laboratory, not just its market

text: **Best-of-breed partnership over vertical integration.** Motorola's edge, in his framing, is not doing everything itself but assembling category leaders into one product: "Entendemos que somos a melhor empresa em tecnologia, mas não em tudo. Por isso, fomos buscar empresas que são referência em suas áreas de atuação. Então, a Motorola é um ecossistema que compila o melhor de cada experiência em um único produto." [We understand we're the best company in technology, but not in everything. That's why we went looking for companies that are the reference in their fields. So Motorola is an ecosystem that compiles the best of each experience into a single product.] (Mobile Time) — instantiated concretely via Bose (audio), Sony (cameras), Corning (glass/screens) and Pantone (color/design), later joined by Swarovski (the "Collections" jeweled line) and the Swiss fragrance house Firmenich (scented packaging) in earlier reporting (NeoFeed).
quotes: Entendemos que somos a melhor empresa em tecnologia, mas não em tudo. Por isso, fomos buscar empresas que são referência em suas áreas de atuação. Então, a Motorola é um ecossistema que compila o melhor de cada experiência em um único produto.
title: Best-of-breed partnership over vertical integration

text: **Rational trust first, aspirational appeal second — a deliberate sequence, not a simultaneous push.** "Nós conseguimos perceber em pesquisas [com grupos de consumidores] elementos muito importantes de confiabilidade, como uma marca com produtos com qualidade e durabilidade. Os consumidores têm aspectos racionais muito fortes associados à marca Motorola." [We were able to see in research [with consumer groups] very important elements of trust, like a brand with quality and durable products. Consumers have very strong rational associations with the Motorola brand.] Only once that foundation is asserted as won does he name the next phase: "Nosso próximo passo é ampliar também esse alcance da marca para aspectos aspiracionais, que vão além da questão racional. O produto é muito competitivo, mas não necessariamente é um produto da moda." [Our next step is to also expand the brand's reach into aspirational aspects, beyond the rational question. The product is very competitive, but not necessarily a fashion product.] (Bloomberg Línea) He is willing to put a number on the aspirational deficit and its closing: superpremium purchase-consideration for the Motorola brand moved from 49% to 73% in internal research ("As pesquisas mostram que 49% dos consumidores consideravam a marca Motorola na hora de escolher o próximo smartphone superpremium. Agora está em 73%"), which he frames as the operational form of the underlying goal — "Eu preciso ser número um na cabeça do consumidor" [I need to be number one in the consumer's mind] — mindshare as the leading indicator that must move before volume leadership can follow (Tecnoblog).

text: **Steady, defensible share growth over aggressive, erratic growth.** "Nós temos planos para crescer, mas precisamos dar passos consistentes para não retroagir." [We have plans to grow, but we need to take consistent steps so we don't regress.] (Forbes Brasil)

text: **Gray-market contraband, not Chinese OEMs, is the named top threat.** "O mercado cinza fomenta outros problemas, também de segurança. É uma evasão de divisa muito grande, então hoje, para nós, é uma preocupação." [The gray market fuels other problems, including security ones. It's a very large currency evasion, so today, for us, it's a concern.] (Forbes Brasil) — reported alongside the fact that contraband represented roughly 20% of Brazilian phone sales in 2024, versus roughly 5% market share for Chinese brands (Huawei, Honor, Xiaomi) combined (Forbes Brasil).

title: Gray-market contraband, not Chinese OEMs, is the named top threat

text: **"Brasil como laboratório de tendências" (Brazil as trend laboratory).** Gist: treat the Brazilian market and Brazilian engineering talent not as a downstream recipient of global product decisions but as a proving ground whose output — features, campaigns, retail formats — gets exported upward into the global product line. *Worked example:* the Foto Guiada feature, invented by a Brazil-based product manager, ships as a differentiator on the flagship razr line globally, not just in Brazil (Mobile Time). *Second, earlier example, same shape:* the 2009 Brazilian Android launch is credited with becoming an internal reference point that lifted the Brazilian team's standing inside the global organization (Tele.Síntese) — the same "local proof point becomes global leverage" mechanic, a decade and a half apart. *Third example, the strongest because it is a go-to-market format rather than a feature or a milestone:* Brazil was "palco do projeto-piloto da empresa no varejo" in 2021 — the physical-retail model (Motostores plus 100+ kiosks) was piloted in Brazil before being extended elsewhere (NeoFeed), the literal "test here first, roll out globally" mechanic the whole thesis rests on.
quotes: Brasil como laboratório de tendências
local proof point becomes global leverage
palco do projeto-piloto da empresa no varejo
test here first, roll out globally
title: "Brasil como laboratório de tendências" (Brazil as trend laboratory)

text: **Best-of-breed ecosystem, not vertical build.** Gist: rather than developing camera sensors, audio hardware, display glass or color/design authority internally, source each from the recognized category leader and integrate. *Worked example:* Bose for audio, Sony for cameras, Corning for display glass, Pantone for color and design language — named explicitly as the mechanism by which "a Motorola é um ecossistema que compila o melhor de cada experiência em um único produto" (Mobile Time); extended in earlier reporting to Swarovski-jeweled special editions and Firmenich-designed packaging fragrance as further "best-of-breed" layers of differentiation (NeoFeed). *Same logic applied to AI:* rather than committing to a single generative-AI supplier, MotoAI is described as an aggregation layer orchestrating multiple providers (Copilot, Gemini, Perplexity) on the top-tier Edge and Razr devices (Tele.Síntese) — the "orchestrate several, own none" move carried from hardware components into the software/AI stack.
quotes: a Motorola é um ecossistema que compila o melhor de cada experiência em um único produto
orchestrate several, own none
title: Best-of-breed ecosystem, not vertical build

text: **Physical retail as a proving ground, not just a sales channel.** Gist: treat stores and kiosks as brand-experience and product-experimentation instruments — a place to test formats and launch campaigns — rather than pure distribution, which is also why they read as the vehicle for the 2021 global retail pilot. *Worked example:* the five Motostores (São Paulo, Fortaleza, Curitiba) and 100+ kiosks are described as "ponto de experimentação dos produtos," with the olfactory identity (Firmenich) deployed in those physical spaces and interior-city expansion planned (NeoFeed).
quotes: ponto de experimentação dos produtos,
title: Physical retail as a proving ground, not just a sales channel

text: **"Lifestyle tech": style/design/color as a co-equal axis with specs.** Gist: refuse to compete on technical specification alone; treat design, color and cultural styling as a parallel battleground, because a meaningful share of consumers — Brazilian and younger, by his own framing — buy on style as much as capability. *Worked example:* "Há uma lacuna no mercado, com muitos players focados apenas em tecnologia e configuração," followed immediately by "o consumidor, em especial, o brasileiro e o mais jovem, também gosta do estilo, do design, da cor e de outras características" (NeoFeed) — instantiated in the simultaneous 2023 launch of the razr 40 ultra (foldable, R$6,999) alongside the edge 40 neo (R$2,499) in the Pantone "Peach Fuzz" color-of-the-year finish (NeoFeed), and later in the Signature line's Pantone-paired Olive Green and Black finishes at R$8,999 (Forbes Brasil).
quotes: Há uma lacuna no mercado, com muitos players focados apenas em tecnologia e configuração,
o consumidor, em especial, o brasileiro e o mais jovem, também gosta do estilo, do design, da cor e de outras características
title: "Lifestyle tech": style/design/color as a co-equal axis with specs

text: **Rational-then-aspirational sequencing of brand equity.** Gist: don't spend on image-building until the functional trust case is empirically established; treat the two as sequential investments, not a single simultaneous brand campaign. *Worked example:* citing internal consumer-group research as proof the "rational" box (quality, durability) is already checked, he names the aspirational phase as the deliberate next stage — executed via hiring a former luxury-market communications lead (reported in the same piece, though not in his own words) and via F1 (Motorola named official smartphone partner of the 2025 season) and Brazil-hosted World Cup sponsorships (men's 2026, women's 2027), explicitly framed as tools to close the aspirational gap rather than generic media spend (Bloomberg Línea).
title: Rational-then-aspirational sequencing of brand equity

text: **Premium mix as a margin/FX-exposure equalizer** *(dossier's inference from adjacent reported facts, not a framework Vidigal names outright — flagged as such).* The reporting notes that roughly 80% of components are imported even though final assembly is 100% domestic, against a year of double-digit dollar appreciation, in the same passage where Vidigal states the mix has shifted from entry-level products toward the R$2,000–R$4,000 band via the Edge and Razr families "para equilibrar os nossos resultados" [to balance out our results] (Bloomberg Línea). The dossier reads this as an implicit hedge-through-mix strategy; Vidigal's own words assert the balancing effect on results, not the FX mechanism explicitly.
quotes: para equilibrar os nossos resultados
title: Premium mix as a margin/FX-exposure equalizer

text: **Move first under regulatory ambiguity; formalize compliance as you go, rather than wait for the rulebook.** Documented from his own career, not from Motorola: launching Brazil's first prepaid plan in 1998 before any prepaid regulation existed, operating under a provisional license and filing monthly reports to Anatel until the framework caught up (Tele.Síntese).
title: Move first under regulatory ambiguity; formalize compliance as you go, rather than wait for the rulebook

text: **Rank threats explicitly, and don't assume the obvious rival is the biggest one.** Names gray-market contraband (~20% of 2024 sales) ahead of Chinese-brand competition (~5% combined share) as the company's top concern, tying it to currency evasion and security risk rather than pure lost-revenue framing (Forbes Brasil).
title: Rank threats explicitly, and don't assume the obvious rival is the biggest one

text: **Treat new entrants as legitimate competitors under shared rules, not as a threat to be resisted.** On Chinese brands (Honor, Oppo) entering the mid-tier where Motorola is strong: "Já conhecemos essas marcas de outros mercados e não há problemas, desde que a disputa seja dentro das mesmas regras," and "no fim do dia, quem compete com Samsung e Apple compete com Honor e Oppo" (NeoFeed) — i.e., competing at the top tier structurally implies competing at every tier beneath it, so there's no separate defensive posture needed for the mid-tier incursion.
quotes: Já conhecemos essas marcas de outros mercados e não há problemas, desde que a disputa seja dentro das mesmas regras,
no fim do dia, quem compete com Samsung e Apple compete com Honor e Oppo
title: Treat new entrants as legitimate competitors under shared rules, not as a threat to be resisted

text: **When a financing tool no longer fits the current positioning, kill it rather than patch it — then look for a new vehicle for the same job.** Motorola discontinued phone-upgrade financing plans specifically because they were incompatible with the shift toward the premium segment, and only later revisited the underlying need through a different mechanism (the Dimo digital account) rather than reviving the original program (NeoFeed; Bloomberg Línea). His candid first-person account of why is more damning of the original tool than the corporate paraphrase: pressed on why Motorola doesn't run an Itaú-style 21-installment iPhone program, he answers that the earlier upgrade plans were killed partly because "muitas vezes o cliente acaba pagando mais caro do que se comprasse um telefone novo. Tivemos algumas reclamações" [often the customer ends up paying more than if they'd just bought a new phone. We had some complaints] — a kill decision driven by customer-harm/complaint evidence, not only by positioning, with the current substitutes named as carrier partnerships and trade-in-based upgrade offers rather than a revived installment plan (Tecnoblog).
quotes: muitas vezes o cliente acaba pagando mais caro do que se comprasse um telefone novo. Tivemos algumas reclamações
title: When a financing tool no longer fits the current positioning, kill it rather than patch it — then look for a new vehicle for the same job

text: **Keep the portfolio to a few "winners" per price band — and treat a bloated SKU list as a defect to correct, not a strategy.** "A gente sempre teve uma estratégia de oferecer poucos produtos, mas que fossem vencedores nas suas faixas de preços... Não adianta ter 15 modelos que entregam proposta de valor similar. Eu tenho que ter um produto realmente vencedor em cada faixa de preço." [We always had a strategy of offering few products, but ones that were winners in their price bands... There's no point having 15 models that deliver a similar value proposition. I have to have a genuinely winning product in each price band.] The heuristic is legible precisely because he documents having violated it under duress and reverted: pandemic component shortages forced a proliferation of near-identical SKUs (G32, G42, G52, G22) to hedge supply risk, and once supply normalized he explicitly returned to the few-winners rule — "Estamos voltando para essa estratégia agora" (Tecnoblog). He also frames launch cadence as demand-driven rather than fixed: he tracks six price bands that "se movimenta de acordo com o poder aquisitivo do brasileiro" and populates the portfolio to the size of each band rather than to a target model count (Tecnoblog).
quotes: A gente sempre teve uma estratégia de oferecer poucos produtos, mas que fossem vencedores nas suas faixas de preços... Não adianta ter 15 modelos que entregam proposta de valor similar. Eu tenho que ter um produto realmente vencedor em cada faixa de preço.
Estamos voltando para essa estratégia agora
se movimenta de acordo com o poder aquisitivo do brasileiro
title: Keep the portfolio to a few "winners" per price band — and treat a bloated SKU list as a defect to correct, not a strategy

text: **Sequence brand investment: prove the functional case before buying the aspirational one.** Applied consistently: resolve "confiabilidade" (reliability) and "durabilidade" first, backed by consumer research, before allocating spend to sponsorships or design collaborations meant to buy aspirational cachet (Bloomberg Línea).
title: Sequence brand investment: prove the functional case before buying the aspirational one

text: **Grow the top of the portfolio without destabilizing the base.** Explicit language of consolidation before expansion — "consistent steps" rather than share-chasing sprints — applied to a portfolio that must defend an already-won intermediate-tier position (34.2% share by NeoFeed's Jan/2024 figure) while separately building premium share nearly from scratch (Forbes Brasil; NeoFeed).
title: Grow the top of the portfolio without destabilizing the base

text: **Focus vs. diversify (within the product portfolio).** Documented, explicit: rather than diversifying into new device categories, the stated bet is a narrower vertical push into the ultra-premium tier via the Signature line (R$8,999, one unit per year planned, Pantone-paired finishes) layered on top of an existing three-tier structure (Moto G / Edge / Razr) (Forbes Brasil; Tele.Síntese).
title: Focus vs. diversify (within the product portfolio)

text: **Build vs. partner (capability sourcing).** Documented, explicit and named repeatedly across interviews: partner with category leaders (Bose, Sony, Corning, Pantone, Swarovski, Firmenich) rather than build audio, camera, display or design-authority capability internally (Mobile Time; NeoFeed).
title: Build vs. partner (capability sourcing)

text: **Local manufacture vs. import.** Documented position: domestic production is the default for the Brazilian lineup, with a single, openly acknowledged temporary exception — the moto pen ultra, imported "por ora" [for now] (Mobile Time) — rather than a blanket import policy or a blanket nationalization claim without exception.
title: Local manufacture vs. import

text: **Financing as a sales lever vs. financing as a pure risk-management function.** Documented: the Dimo digital wallet (installment financing up to 18x, interest 2.99%–6.99% a.m., >2.5 million wallet users as of the reporting) is used deliberately to move premium-tier units (R$2,000–R$3,000 ticket) in physical retail, with digital-channel expansion planned via partnerships with Jazz Tech and Banco Arbi (BaaS) (Bloomberg Línea).
title: Financing as a sales lever vs. financing as a pure risk-management function

text: **Marketing spend allocation: sponsorship vs. generic media.** Documented: F1 (Motorola as official smartphone partner for the 2025 season, part of Lenovo's elevation to "global partner" status) and World Cup sponsorships (men's 2026, women's 2027, both hosted partly in Brazil) are named specifically as tools to close the "aspirational" brand gap — not generic advertising spend (Bloomberg Línea).
title: Marketing spend allocation: sponsorship vs. generic media

text: **Pricing/segmentation by price band, with explicit share targets per band.** Documented, granular: intermediate (<R$2,000, 35.9% share, already dominated), premium (R$2,000–R$3,000, 14.6% share vs. 72% Samsung / 15% Apple), super-premium (>R$3,000, 2% share vs. 72% Apple / 25% Samsung) — the stated strategic focus follows directly from this map, targeting the premium and super-premium gaps rather than the already-won intermediate tier (NeoFeed).
title: Pricing/segmentation by price band, with explicit share targets per band

text: **Raise vs. bootstrap.** Not applicable in the founder sense — Vidigal runs a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lenovo-owned Motorola Mobility, not an independent venture; no capital-raising decision is documented or would be his to make. Recorded as a structural non-fit rather than a documented position (see *Provenance notes*).
title: Raise vs. bootstrap

text: **When to fire / when to sell.** Not documented in this corpus. The only personnel transition on record is his own appointment in September 2023, succeeding José Cardoso, who was promoted to lead Motorola's Latin America operation — a succession-as-promotion, not a termination (NeoFeed). No source touches a firing, restructuring, or divestiture decision under his presidency.
title: When to fire / when to sell

text: **Pivot vs. persevere.** Documented, first-person, and — unusually for this corpus — a genuine deviate-and-revert rather than a straight-line story. The durable strategy is "poucos produtos vencedores por faixa de preço"; Vidigal describes abandoning it under the pandemic component shortage (proliferating near-duplicate Moto G SKUs — G32, G42, G52, G22 — to keep at least one buildable if a supplier failed), then explicitly reverting once supply normalized: "Estamos voltando para essa estratégia agora" (Tecnoblog). This is the cleanest pivot/persevere case in the corpus — a temporary, externally-forced departure from a stated principle, consciously reversed — and it reads as persevere-on-principle, pivot-on-tactics. The financing-plan discontinuation (see *Decision heuristics*) is a second, adjacent data point but a weaker one, since the underlying premium direction it served was never in question.
quotes: poucos produtos vencedores por faixa de preço
Estamos voltando para essa estratégia agora
title: Pivot vs. persevere

text: Across every interview in this corpus, Vidigal's default register is data-forward and sequencing-driven: he answers questions in percentages, price bands and rank claims ("terceiro maior mercado," "quarto maior mercado," "34,2% de participação," "15% a 18%," "R$ 2.000 a R$ 4.000") rather than in adjectives or vision-statement abstractions. His signature rhetorical move is a named two-stage sequence — rational before aspirational, consolidation before new-store-equivalent growth ("passos consistentes para não retroagir"), local proof-of-concept before global rollout — stated explicitly as an order of operations rather than left implicit. He is conspicuously non-confrontational about direct competitors: Chinese entrants are folded into "as mesmas regras," never named as a threat in the way gray-market contraband is; when he does name a concern (contraband, currency evasion), the language sharpens noticeably ("evasão de divisa muito grande," "preocupação"). He repeats the same core facts — Brazil's market rank, the R&D engineer headcount, the specific example of a Brazilian-built feature — across interviews spanning at least three years (2024–2026) with only minor numeric updates, suggesting a deliberately maintained, consistent talking-point set rather than off-the-cuff answers; this is corporate-spokesperson discipline more than personal color. The one moment of self-reference beyond the corporate voice is procedural and historical, not personal or emotional: recounting his own 1998 decision to launch under a provisional telecom license before regulation existed, told as evidence of a comfort with calculated regulatory risk rather than as a personal narrative. The earliest interview (Tecnoblog, Nov/2023) is the only one where the register loosens under live questioning: he lets an anecdote in ("fui rodar durante a Black Friday e passei pelo Shopping Itaquera... os clientes perguntavam se tinha 5G. Eu pensava comigo mesmo: para usar onde?"), deflects a pointed cost question with humour twice marked "(risos)" ("Resolveria a nossa vida se fosse só reduzir R$ 100"), and concedes a competitive gap plainly when pushed on why Motorola can't run an Itaú/iPhone-style installment program ("Nós ainda não estamos neste estágio. Temos que trabalhar para chegar lá") — the closest the corpus comes to an unscripted, self-aware voice, and a reason a future refresh should prioritise more live Q&A and video over press paraphrase.

text: How this figure diverges from other named council members on specific questions. Largely inferred from each side's separately documented record — no source shows Vidigal naming or responding to any of these figures directly, flagged accordingly.

**vs. Manoel Conde Neto (Farma Conde) — best-of-breed partnership vs. vertical integration as the growth engine.** Conde Neto's stated next-decade bet is building an in-house pharmaceutical manufacturing lab specifically to take private label from 15% to 50% of revenue — vertical integration as the margin/independence lever. Vidigal's repeatedly stated model is the opposite instinct applied to a comparable premiumization problem: rather than build camera, audio or display capability in-house, Motorola explicitly imports category leaders (Bose, Sony, Corning, Pantone) and integrates them ("a Motorola é um ecossistema que compila o melhor de cada experiência"). Same generic problem — how does a mid-market brand fund its move upmarket — opposite make-or-buy answer. (Mobile Time; cf. Conde Neto dossier, Sincofarma SP)

text: **vs. Jensen Huang (Nvidia) — ecosystem strategy from opposite starting points.** Huang's documented model is to "create a thing vertically and then... open it horizontally so everybody could use whatever piece they would like" — build the core stack first, then trade full-stack monetization for reach. Vidigal never builds the core components at all; the ecosystem is assembled from day one out of externally-owned category leaders (Bose/Sony/Corning/Pantone), and the "compile the best of each" framing is presented as Motorola's structural identity, not a later concession. Both converge on "ecosystem breadth over solo ownership" as the source of value, but one arrives there by opening what it built, the other by never building it. (Mobile Time; cf. Huang dossier, Stratechery 2026)

text: **vs. Denis Benchimol Minev (Bemol) — the Zona Franca de Manaus as backdrop, read from opposite chairs.** Minev is a policy voice defending the Manaus Free Trade Zone and Amazon-region industrial policy from outside the consumer-electronics sector, arguing the region needs a national-scale ambition and pro-paving/pro-Zona-Franca positions to attract investment. Vidigal is a direct operator inside that same zone — Motorola manufactures domestically (reporting cites Jaguariúna and Manaus) — and treats near-total domestic production as the operating default, with a single named, openly-acknowledged import exception (the moto pen ultra) rather than a policy argument about the zone itself. One is arguing for the conditions that make manufacturing in the region viable; the other is a tenant of those conditions making a much narrower make-or-buy call within them. (Mobile Time; cf. Minev dossier, O Globo/JCAM)
title: vs. Denis Benchimol Minev (Bemol) — the Zona Franca de Manaus as backdrop, read from opposite chairs

text: **vs. Frederico Trajano (Magazine Luiza) — direction of the innovation-transfer arrow.** Trajano's documented playbook explicitly imports strategic models from abroad into Brazil in named cycles (Silicon Valley cloud/digitization, then China's superapp/fintech integration — "aprendizado por imersão"). Vidigal's central, repeated claim runs the opposite direction: Brazilian-built product features and Brazilian go-to-market experiments are exported *from* Brazil *to* the rest of Motorola's global lineup (the Foto Guiada example; the "maior exportadora de tecnologia para o mundo" framing). Same generic move — treat a market as a place to learn playbooks — opposite direction of the arrow. (Mobile Time; Bloomberg Línea; cf. Trajano dossier, Forbes Brasil/GV Executivo)

text: **Market-share figures are internally inconsistent across sources and don't reconcile.** Forbes Brasil (Mar/2026) cites 27.5% share and "sexto trimestre consecutivo" of vice-leadership behind Samsung, with a stated goal of 30% by end of 2026; NeoFeed (Jan/2024) cites 34.2% share as second place; Bloomberg Línea (Dec/2024) cites "30% em volume" for second place; and StatCounter data reported by Oficina da Net (Nov/2025) — a wholly independent, web-traffic-based methodology — puts Motorola at just 17% in October 2025, having only just "voltado a superar" Apple for second place after briefly losing it in September 2025. These are plausibly different methodologies (company-reported activations/sell-in vs. StatCounter's browser-usage panel) and possibly different measurement bases (value vs. volume), but the corpus does not reconcile them, and the month-to-month StatCounter volatility complicates the "sustained, consistent advance since 2013" narrative repeated in the institutional interviews. Recorded as an open ambiguity, not resolved. (Forbes Brasil; NeoFeed; Bloomberg Línea; Oficina da Net)

text: **Almost no adversarial press targets him or his tenure specifically.** Every source with his own quotes in this corpus is an access-granted business-press interview (Mobile Time, Tele.Síntese, Forbes Brasil, Bloomberg Línea, NeoFeed, Tecnoblog) or a promotional listing (AIoT Brasil). The Tecnoblog factory-visit Q&A (Nov/2023) is the one partial exception: it does put real follow-up pushback to him — "Não deu certo?" on the failed financing program, "Não tem aparelho demais?" on SKU bloat, and a skeptical probe on whether 5G demand is real — and he answers candidly rather than deflecting, but it remains a sympathetic, invited-to-the-factory interview, not an analyst rebuttal or an investigative piece. No source in the corpus places an independent critic's claim directly against his and asks him to answer it. The one substantive critique available (Canaltech, Mar/2022) — camera-quality gaps relative to specs, slower Android-update commitments than Samsung's Galaxy A line, confusing Moto G-series naming across 18 launches in a single year — predates his September 2023 appointment by 18 months and never names him; it is used here as a documented structural gap (camera and software-update parity) that his ultra-premium push still has to answer for, not as personal criticism of him. text: **The premiumization pitch implicitly concedes a brand-relevance deficit.** The push to raise premium share from 10% to a stated 30%-in-"próximos anos" ambition, and the explicit "aspirational" investment phase, is itself evidence that a meaningful slice of younger consumers hold, at best, "apenas uma vaga lembrança" [only a faint memory] tied to the dated "Hello, Moto" slogan — a framing the Bloomberg Línea piece itself notes. Vidigal's own sequencing logic (rational-then-aspirational) is, read this way, an implicit admission that the brand currently under-indexes on relevance with the very demographic the premium and lifestyle-tech strategy targets. (Bloomberg Línea)

title: The premiumization pitch implicitly concedes a brand-relevance deficit

text: **A labor-practice controversy exists in the same industrial ecosystem but is explicitly not attributable to him.** A 2020 denunciation by the Sindicato dos Metalúrgicos do Amazonas (Sindmetal-AM) accused Flextronics da Amazônia — a contract manufacturer described in that piece as producing Motorola products — of suspending contracts while simultaneously hiring 200+ temporary workers, cutting pay, running crowded pandemic-era buses, and at least three Covid-19 worker deaths. text: Rony Meisler is the co-founder of Reserva, the irreverent Brazilian menswear brand he bootstrapped from R$6,000 and door-to-door shorts into a roughly R$2B AR&Co before a turbulent 2024 exit from Azzas 2154 (the 2020 sale to Arezzo&Co was ~R$715M, mostly in locked-up shares); he now runs Rebels Ventures, a club-deal investor and self-described "copiloto" in consumer brands, media and entrepreneur education, sells the "Manual de Donos" newsletter school, and chairs Conscious Capitalism Brazil. His lens is **brand-as-movement and brand as the scarce asset when everything commoditizes**: audience, then community, then product (the ACP funnel) with near-zero launch risk; the customer, and the salesperson closest to them, as the real boss; cash over the P&L; and purpose as a profit engine, argued against Milton Friedman by name. He is contrarian on disruption worship, the lone genius, the do-what-you-love creed (he says do what you are good at), mentoring and info-product gurus, and Silicon Valley dividend orthodoxy (he now says founders should take dividends and live as owners), and he is openly a curator-synthesist who credits Sinek, Youngme Moon, Jack Welch, Rory Sutherland and his father. He aligns with brand-builders like caito-maia, luiz-seabra and, personally, his self-described "madrinha" luiza-helena-trajano, and clashes with numbers-first operators (frederico-trajano), centralizing controllers (the Birman split, though he now says "nunca teve briga"), and Friedman-style investors; the real tensions are a founder fused to his brand and a control friction he admits to, a history of brand controversies defended on intent first (2014 to 2022) plus the 2023 Fluminense "pó de arroz" suit, theatrical pranks beside an authenticity thesis, and many self-reported numbers that drift from one telling to the next.

text:
Rony Meisler (b. March 4, 1981, Rio de Janeiro) is a production engineer by training (PUC-RJ) who became one of Brazil's best-known brand entrepreneurs. He and advertising-trained childhood friend Fernando Sigal noticed, at a gym, five men wearing the identical pair of shorts without registering it, the moment he calls **"O dia D"** (for "demanda reprimida" [pent-up demand]), and read it as evidence of a "multidão faminta" [hungry crowd] of Brazilian men underserved by fashion (blog, "É para isso que eu pago a internet"). In 2006 (Catraca Livre, Poder360 and meusucesso say 2004; his own dated statements, his LinkedIn profile and the 18th anniversary he marked on 6 September 2024 point to 2006) they founded **Reserva** with just R$6,000 ("Começamos nosso negócio em 2006 apenas com R$ 6 mil e esse foi o total da grana que investimos até hoje", "Don't look up!"), selling shorts door to door, then to multi-brand resellers, before opening a first 33m² store on Rua Maria Quitéria in Ipanema, later enlarged to 66m² ("Don't look up!"). His father, Luiz Meisler (Oracle's VP for Latin America), had talked him out of over-engineered projections: "Esqueçam essa planilha e vão para rua criar produtos incríveis" (blog, "Roube um estilo de liderança"). Twelve years after the first store, Fast Company named Reserva among the world's most innovative companies alongside the "big 4," citing 1P=5P (hunger relief), a 45-day paternity leave, the customer-customization system *faça.vc*, print-on-demand, and *"cara ou coroa"*, a program employing people over 70 in its stores ("Don't look up!"). By 2019 revenue reached ~R$400M.
In December 2020 **Arezzo&Co acquired Reserva for ~R$715M**. His own account of the rationale is a market-sizing one: Reserva's brand awareness was "AB+" but its retail reach far narrower, making the addressable market "10 vezes maior" [10x bigger] under a bigger platform (TalksbyLeo #238, unofficial captions). He became CEO of **AR&Co** (Reserva, Reserva Mini, Reserva Go, Reserva Ink, Eva, Oficina, later Baw), co-led a ~R$900M follow-on at R$83/share with Alexandre Birman, and grew the division from about R$400M (2019) to a reported ~R$2B (Sicomércio and Startups.com.br coverage; the company's own August 2024 communiqué cited R$1.6B through June 2024, per Bloomberg Línea), with margins he describes as rising from 10 to 12% to 16 to 17% (self-reported, Futurum Talks). At the sale his father warned him that founders who sell often "sabem que elas venderam, mas elas não entendem que elas venderam" [know they sold it but don't understand they sold it], advice he says he tried to live by for four years.
He left Azzas 2154 in 2024: the departure was announced on 29 August 2024, the founders stayed "até o final deste ano" to support the transition (Azzas's wording, per Bloomberg Línea), and he dates his own exit to 31 December 2024 (Entusiasta, unofficial captions; see *Provenance notes*). The press framed it as turbulent, with a compensation gap and a centralization clash with Birman after the Arezzo and Soma merger; he frames it as knowing when to stop and says there was never a fight (see *Positions by decision type* and *Blind spots*). A failing health checkup (pre-diabetic, pre-hypertensive, ~20kg overweight, high cortisol; he dates it to the end of 2023) became the trigger for **Rebels Ventures** (2025), a hybrid investment/advisory/venture-builder that began in wellness and longevity, run with Fernando Sigal, José Alberto Silva and Jayme Nigri Moszkowicz. He has chaired **Conscious Capitalism Brazil** since 2016 (alongside Hugo Bethlem), and co-authored **"Rebeldes Têm Asas"** with journalist Sérgio Pugliese (2017; special edition with a bonus chapter and a preface by Luiza Helena Trajano, Editora Gente, 2021, which debuted at no. 1 on the PublishNews general list with 5,540 copies in a week).
**After Azzas.** He took about 30 days off in California with his family before producing content (Entusiasta, unofficial captions), staged the "Doing Nothing Club" prank, and launched Rebels Ventures publicly in 2025 with a first announced bet on The Simple Gym (Exame, May 2025; Fitfeed, June 2025). By July 2026 he reports eight portfolio companies, R$78M invested from partners' own capital, a personal-brand newsletter ("E-mail do Rony"), a paid email school for small owners ("Manual de Donos"), and a fashion non-compete that ends on 4 December 2026 (Café com Ferri; Excepcionais, unofficial captions). Before entrepreneurship he had only a brief Accenture internship and no executive role; the Startups.com.br summary reports that he called becoming an executive after the sale "o maior desafio da vida até aqui". In September 2024 he marked Reserva's 18th anniversary with a pay-what-you-want sale of the book (R$1.80, R$18 or R$180; 1,800 copies; all proceeds to social projects, with promised accountability), his own promotional text (Substack, Skeelo).
Disambiguation: the working brief referenced a book titled *"Rebeldria."* No such Meisler title exists; his book is *Rebeldes Têm Asas*. An earlier brief also referenced *"Não Espere o Vento Mudar"* (a sailing aphorism, not his) and a "Movimento Black Comedy" program (unverified). His flagship social program is **1P=5P** (below). These are flagged, not fabricated.

text: **Time ownership is the real wealth, and being an executive cost him it.** On the four years after the sale: *"alguém era dono do meu tempo e não eu. E isso me matou, cara."* [someone else owned my time, not me, and that killed me] and *"o problema não era trabalhar, o problema era não ser dono do meu tempo"* (Entusiasta, unofficial captions). On why he left: *"a decisão ela não foi de saída, ela não foi financeira, a decisão foi para recuperar isso"* [the decision wasn't about leaving or about money, it was about recovering this] (Excepcionais, unofficial captions). text: **Start with what you are good at, not what you love.** *"faz o que você é bom"* [do what you are good at]: in the first phase of a company "faz o que você ama" is, in his view, a myth, and small daily wins release the dopamine that creates the love afterwards: *"Se você fizer o que você é bom, quando você vencer a primeira, as vitórias pequenas do dia a dia, vai liberar a dopamina"* (ROI Hunters #349, unofficial captions). This reverses an older line used to promote his talks: *"O empreendedor não perde tempo pensando em que negócio investir, ele faz uma paixão se tornar algo rentável"* [the entrepreneur doesn't waste time choosing a business; he makes a passion profitable] (PANROTAS event announcement, January 2025, an undated pull quote). Treat the 2026 spoken version as current.

text: **Purpose is discovered by trying and failing, not decreed in a meeting.** *"A palavra do momento é o propósito."* and *"Agora, quando é a pessoa jurídica, ela acha que vai entrar em uma sala de reunião e já sair de lá com o propósito. Mas não é assim, é preciso errar para aprender"* [Companies think they'll walk into a meeting room and walk out with a purpose. It doesn't work like that; you have to err to learn.] His analogy: an individual finds what fulfils them through years of therapy (PANROTAS 2025, reporter-attributed quotes). This refines, and partly softens, the purpose-as-profit-engine line above.

Não tem como inovar se não errar."* [we learn when we get it wrong; you can't innovate without getting it wrong] (PANROTAS 2025, to a travel-agency audience; the reporter paraphrases that many people feel obliged to disrupt the market and see themselves as losers if they don't).

text: **Stakeholder capitalism is a longevity claim, not only a moral one.** *"As empresas que estarão vivas daqui a 200, 300 ou 400 anos são as que pregam o capitalismo de stakeholder e não de shareholder"* and *"O dia que eu estiver aqui para olhar apenas o resultado financeiro, eu não verei mais sentido no negócio"* [The day I am here only to look at the financial result, I will no longer see meaning in the business] (Diário do Comércio column by Juliane Maciel, a Conscious Capitalism ambassador, who says she took the lines from an IstoÉ Dinheiro interview that this pass could not locate; treat as second-hand, from the period when he was still AR&Co CEO).

text: **Never depend on other people's money.** Rony traces the rule to a failed corporate-barter website he built at 18, when an investor who had promised funds backed out in the dot-com bubble: *"Nunca mais ia depender dinheiro de ninguém para fazer minhas coisas."* [I would never again depend on anyone's money to do my things.] (Entusiasta, unofficial captions). His father's version, as he retells it: *"Vai inventar um modelo que se sustenta, porque dinheiro de pai e nem de banco você vai tomar"* [Invent a model that sustains itself, because you won't get money from your father or from a bank] (Café com Ferri, unofficial captions).

title: Never depend on other people's money

text: **Audience → Community → Product (ACP funnel).** Build the audience, convert it into a community with shared values, then launch products that funnel already wants, near-zero CAC. *Worked example:* he calls it *"um funil que é mais velho que a nossa avó"* [a funnel older than our grandmother] but says Reserva's entire management model *"Era ancorado no ACP, porque assim a gente garante que a empresa inteira trabalha pro cliente"* [was anchored in ACP, so the whole company works for the customer], and that the same audience-first logic sourced Rebels Ventures' first investment: *"Eu comecei a treinar o algoritmo para me mostrar negócios assim"* [I started training the algorithm to show me businesses like that], until The Simple Gym appeared in his timeline as a lead rather than a pitch (TalksbyLeo #238, unofficial captions). Caveat, from the "Community is the new king" post: *"quando o “creator” é também empreendedor, a história muda"*, audience alone isn't a business.
quotes: um funil que é mais velho que a nossa avó
Era ancorado no ACP, porque assim a gente garante que a empresa inteira trabalha pro cliente
Eu comecei a treinar o algoritmo para me mostrar negócios assim
Community is the new king
title: Audience → Community → Product (ACP funnel)

text: **Three leverages: Capital, Code, Content.** Scaling needs leverage: Capital (not accessible to all), Code (micro-SaaS, cheaper via AI), Content (most accessible). *Worked example, the "vibe coding" pivot:* a Rebels-backed educator had emotional attachment to a "Micro SaaS" course brand priced to sell at R$97 "one shot"; Meisler talked him into repositioning around AI "vibe coding" and repricing, by his account the relaunch sold nearly R$2 million in 48 hours (captions: *"A gente vendeu quase R$ 2 milhõesais em 48 horas, Léo."*, followed by *"O Bruno vendeu."*; TalksbyLeo #238, unofficial captions, founder-reported). This is Content/Code leverage exercised directly on a portfolio company, not just stated as thesis.
quotes: A gente vendeu quase R$ 2 milhõesais em 48 horas, Léo.
O Bruno vendeu.
title: Three leverages: Capital, Code, Content

text: **Rebels Ventures' operating model: "copiloto," not owner.** Investment + advisory + venture-builder, structured as a **club deal** (each partner sizes their own check per deal, no obligation) on bootstrapped businesses already at market fit (the bands moved over time, see *Positions by decision type*), deliberately *not* Rocket-Internet-style building from zero. *Worked example:* *"É o mesmo framework de quando estávamos na Reserva e depois na AR&Co. Mas quem manda no negócio é o empreendedor. Estaremos como copilotos se ele precisar"* (NeoFeed, Rebels exclusive), with the four partners split by function (Rony on brand, Jayme on operations, Fernando on supply chain, José on digital). His limits are under *Selection by edge* below; how the copilot role works in practice is under *Rebels' operating mode*.
quotes: É o mesmo framework de quando estávamos na Reserva e depois na AR&Co. Mas quem manda no negócio é o empreendedor. Estaremos como copilotos se ele precisar
title: Rebels Ventures' operating model: "copiloto," not owner

text: **CX as a variable cost / journey reverse-engineering.** Treat experience design as a margin lever: *"Este varejista que vos escreve sempre viu CX como custo variável."* Sequence the journey so high-margin, customizable choices come first (blog, "A ordem dos fatores...").

title: CX as a variable cost / journey reverse-engineering

text: **"Seja a cola" (be the glue): the Battier effect.** The most valuable operator is the connective, unglamorous force who makes the team better, not the solo star. *Worked example:* NBA role-player Shane Battier, *"Quando eu ajudava os outros a vencer, eu deixava de ser o estranho. Eu me tornava parte."* (blog, "Seja a cola"). The thesis sits in friction with his own admitted difficulty ceding decisions at Rebels (see *Blind spots*).

Quando eu ajudava os outros a vencer, eu deixava de ser o estranho. Eu me tornava parte.
Seja a cola
title: "Seja a cola" (be the glue): the Battier effect

text: **Innovation ≠ technology; validate cheap before you scale capital, "tinta amarela."** *Worked example:* a store-display manager wanted to repaint every storefront yellow at a cost of "algumas centenas de milhares de reais," certain it would lift sales. Instead of funding it directly, Meisler had her test-paint only the chain's *worst-performing* store, brokered a bulk discount from a paint brand contingent on the rollout, and let the pilot's result (the store *"dobrou o faturamento em muito pouco tempo"*) decide the full spend. *"Tem gente que gosta de chamar esse teste de MVP, mas eu gosto de chamar de teste a custo baixo mesmo."* (blog, "Tinta amarela").
